rulings.evidence: REFUSED the board's deli-ham bridge: deli ham is sliced lunch meat at several dollars a pound and diced-ham is a convenience pack, while this is a 7-9 lb bone-in whole ham at a fraction of that per pound - a different product concept AND a different price class. Proposed as a new id.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: The board answers this phrase with deli-ham (7 of 7), which is sliced sandwich meat sold by the half pound - a different product and a much higher price per pound than a whole bone-in spiral-sliced ham sold at 7-9 lb. The vocabulary's other ham row, diced-ham, is a diced convenience pack, also a different price class. Searched by food and not by string: neither a lunch-meat id nor a diced id can carry a whole holiday ham. If the estate already prices whole hams under a spelling such as 'ham' or 'bone-in-ham', alias there instead.
